description: Runs the heating and cooling of one room in Home Assistant and forecasts the time, energy and cost to reach its target.

glossary.cool threshold: The room temperature above which the AC cools. It comes from the preset, your target, the price and occupancy.
glossary.heat target: The room temperature the heater aims at.
glossary.heat threshold: The heat target minus 0.5 K. A PID heater and AC heat start below it.
glossary.preset: One of comfort, eco, boost and away. Each has its own cool threshold and heat target.
glossary.tick: One run of the control loop. It happens every 5 minutes and after each change on the room thermostat.
glossary.restart delay: The time a device stays off before it may start again, 3 minutes by default.
glossary.room model: The three learned values k, c and g that describe how the room gains heat and how the AC cools it.
glossary.observe only: The state of an entry with control off. It learns and forecasts and sends no commands.
glossary.automatic mode: The thermostat mode in which the room runs whatever it needs. Home Assistant names it heat_cool in a room that can heat and cool, and auto in a room that only cools.
glossary.area: A Home Assistant area, such as Bedroom. A room entry can belong to one: setup suggests the area's entities, and the room's thermostat and sensors are placed in it.
glossary.action: What Home Assistant called a service before 2024.8, such as hvac_horizon.set_lock. Call one from Developer tools > Actions or from an automation.
